answer: A factory can pack a jury if new names leave no lasting artifact. Each recruit books a slot at the public forge, strikes one copper die that only its key can heat, and seats the mark in a numbered marble slab held on a two-epoch shelf. The cost is the booked slot plus a locked shelf fee, which one shop cannot schedule for a thousand aliases overnight. Peers replay the forge log, match the die hash to one key, and reject any slab whose copper mark repeats or whose number was already seated. It fails if dies can be borrowed or slots faked, so a clash melts the fee and voids the slab.
